fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The little man in the flask", "body": "Chance Garton brings back Juan Ayala, host of The Juan On Juan Podcast, to unpack the homunculus, the artificial little man of alchemy. Juan explains that the word itself is Latin for little man and that it did not enter the vocabulary until the sixteenth century with Paracelsus, the eccentric father of modern toxicology whose life Philip Ball chronicles in The Devil's Doctor. Paracelsus gave the first actual recipe. Earlier versions existed under other names, including the anthroparion of Zosimos that Carl Jung later wrote about, and the airborne creation Simon Magus boasted of."}, {"title": "Spontaneous generation and the limits of observing", "body": "The episode circles the old doctrine of spontaneous generation, the belief that maggots came from rotting meat and lice from a moist body. Juan links it to preformationism and Aristotelian biology, which survived into the eighteenth century, and to the conviction that tiny men sat crouched inside sperm waiting for the right conditions to sprout. He uses this to argue that pure observation misleads people, which is why he cannot follow the flat earth movement. Chance counters that calculation misleads too, and describes gnats appearing inside his parents' cabinet around forgotten potatoes."}, {"title": "The homunculus your doctor already recognizes", "body": "Juan points out that mainstream neuroscience keeps its own homunculus, the cortical map sometimes drawn as cortex man, which sizes each body part by how much brain territory controls it. Because that map shifts with habit and trauma, everyone's homunculus is different. Chance connects this to biofield anatomy and the tunings he does for clients, where, he says, a person's unconscious self image can carry a withered leg or an area cut off from life force. He also realizes his remote tuning table of crystals laid out as a body is homunculus magic."}, {"title": "Bodies, doubles and stolen driver's seats", "body": "The strangest thread is the Cartesian homunculus, drawn from a 1694 text Juan found that he says contains the first known use of the phrase outer space. In it Rene Descartes sniffs a powder and projects his consciousness to worlds where philosophers keep their own libraries, while a little placeholder runs his body on autopilot. Deep conversation makes it malfunction, and sometimes it refuses to give the body back. Chance compares this to a Daoist watcher, the Picatrix, and African shamanic accounts of an entity guarding the body during a journey."}, {"title": "Artificial persons, data doubles and fatherhood", "body": "Both men bring the idea into the present. Chance argues that the all caps name on a birth certificate is literally an artificial person traded for the placenta, and Juan asks whether corporations have been building sympathetic doubles from the data we hand over, pointing to Purdue's Synthetic Environment for Analysis and Simulation and its sentient world simulation. Juan believes the true magnum opus was never gold but artificial life. The hour closes softly, with Juan describing his two sons and Chance revealing he has a child on the way."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Juan Ayala of the Juan On Juan Podcast returns to InnerVerse to bring forward his research on the mysterious alchemical formation of the homunculus, the alleged process and technique of creating life through artificial means. How can this supremely secretive subject inform us about the origins of humanity, modern AI tech, the generative powers of nature, Jesus and the Brazen Serpent, and the immaculate conceptions of the savior at the onset of each world age?

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Earth as a Macrocosmic Ark", "body": "Chance lays out the flood mythos as a cycle in which the world is destroyed and remade, with the man on the boat as a new Adam, the hull as the yoni and the mast as the phallus. In the macrocosm the Earth itself becomes the ark, since DNA survives in soil for ages and long vanished creatures like triops reappeared after orgone projects brought rain to the Arizona desert. Juan answers with a plate from Edward Kelley showing an alchemical vessel, paired animals, an egg that births the divine homunculus, and Noah's ark tucked in the corner, while Chance reads the mountain as Mount Meru, the world axis."}, {"title": "Cities and Buildings as Living Vessels", "body": "Chance asks whether a city, with resources flowing in, waste flowing out and circuitry running through it, could be a homunculus, noting that Romans would court the god of an enemy town before a siege. Juan brings Marsilio Ficino's account of architects calling their buildings homunculi, where an idea is seeded in the mind like a fetus, born through a scale model and finished as the building itself. He adds Henry Plant calling his hotel a pet, human pillars sealed into foundations, and what he dubs homunculi warfare, rival dynasties racing to build palaces with more rooms and floors, with the Habsburgs entombed at the Escorial."}, {"title": "Technology, Language and the Proto Computer", "body": "Chance wonders whether any closed circuit with enough energy looping through it might take on a kind of soul, which could be what AI really is. Juan shares a page from John Dee's magical journals, Sloane MS 3191, a grid for extracting entity names that looks eerily like a circuit board, and points to daemons and sigils in programming. Drawing on his own CAD work, he notes the Cartesian coordinate system sits at the core of 3D modeling, and proposes the homunculus was a proto computer used for divination. Chance adds that technology originally meant language, the guarded terms of art of every guild."}, {"title": "Three Eras of the Homunculus", "body": "Juan traces how the idea mutated over time, from the Taoist golden man projected out of consciousness to escape samsara, to the alchemical meat and bones creature dissected for its essence, to what he calls the Crowleyan homunculus, an ordinary pregnancy ritually steered to host an invoked entity, laid out in a 1916 text. He links that lineage to programmed doubles and political lookalikes, then to Attack of the Clones, where compliant soldiers are grown on a sea planet and aged quickly, arriving 21 years before the synthetic human headlines. Chance adds the old belief that an expectant mother's imagination shapes what she carries."}, {"title": "Cows, Bees, Honey and a Forbidden Text", "body": "Juan describes hunting the Liber Vaccae, a handwritten work surviving from a fragmented Arabic source through roughly 15 translations whose titles kept changing, until he found 22 pages under another name in which the cow becomes a prophesying talisman. While translating for the Mind Unveiled documentary, the AI refused passages as sacred and dangerous, and human translators declined the job. Chance ties apis, the Latin word for bee, to the Apis bull and beeve to beef, and recalls cow corpses generating bees for magic. Juan closes with the legend of the mellified man, preserved in honey to become a healing elixir, and Nepal's psychedelic mad honey."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I always tell people, with the occult, it doesn't matter if you don't believe in it, but they believe in it.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/c975ca54-711c-4695-b561-cffc1c0b10d2/JUAN-AYALA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If you are using money to survive, you're a part of that creature from Jekyll Island.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/c975ca54-711c-4695-b561-cffc1c0b10d2/JUAN-AYALA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It could be that some cities are intentionally designed to be a type of vessel for an entity.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "So, think about how all this technology we're on right now works. Behind it all is code, is language. Technology and language are inseparable concepts.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In my opinion, it's super strong. Change is always for the better. That's the nature of reality that is self-ordering.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think that life imitates art in this sort of way, and I found it funny that we've all had exposure to the homunculus concept for a very long time.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/c975ca54-711c-4695-b561-cffc1c0b10d2/JUAN-AYALA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The same way they can build these places to elevate your consciousness, they can build them to suppress your consciousness.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/c975ca54-711c-4695-b561-cffc1c0b10d2/JUAN-AYALA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Santa Claus is not a physical thing, but it exists in whatever perceivable reality you're experiencing.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/c975ca54-711c-4695-b561-cffc1c0b10d2/JUAN-AYALA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You're making a copy of something that's perfect, but then your copy's not that perfect.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/c975ca54-711c-4695-b561-cffc1c0b10d2/JUAN-AYALA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think that there could be cats out there that believe we have to burn it all down so that God reboots this thing because it's not that good right now.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "The subject of the homunculus is the study of the conditions in which life may just spontaneously generate as maggots appear on rotting meat and perhaps bees may manifest out of the corpse of a bull.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And again, what I love about alchemy, it's such a beautiful topic because it's, you know, it's physical, biological, psychological and transcendental. And so have your pick, right? The homunculus exists on various levels of existence, quite literally.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "So while your consciousness is projected outside of your body, there's a little Cartesian homunculus that comes and sits down in the past and the driver's seat of your body. And it does the bare minimum for you. It'll brush your teeth. It'll eat for you. It'll go to work for you, whatever.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "And if you read his it's the book by Philip Ball. It's called The Devil's Doctor. And he was at the forefront of mineralogy as well, by the way.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "And, you know, where this also ties into people's everyday lives would be the homunculus that you trade your placenta for at birth, which is your birth-certificated person, your artificial person. That's literally what your all caps name, your identity registered with the government is called an artificial person.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "But what what she ends up saying is that there are underground cities where there are clones of people that actually exist and are currently alive, where they're like repeatedly running crazy simulations like zombie apocalypses and underground cities, fully artificially lit and everything.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "But the artificial creation of life was the true magnum opus because in alchemy, there are various magnum opus. There is the right, the philosopher's stone, the elixir of life. You have the divine androgyn. And then you have the homunculus is one of them, too.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "So the feeling you get when you first see your son or daughter or whatever it is, I have two sons.
